resolves: Stage 1 rev 1 blocking decision D3 (multichannel billing)

the_risk_it_probed.quote: How do you calculate costs for multichannel audio? We bill based on the total duration of processed audio. If you process a 10-minute file with 2 channels (stereo), you are billed for 20 minutes of processing.
the_risk_it_probed.why_it_mattered: 133 of the 230 in-scope units are MP4 video files, which are commonly stereo, and stage-1 rev 1 section 7a remuxes with '-c:a copy', which PRESERVES channel count. The plan would knowingly submit stereo audio at double cost.
the_risk_it_probed.worst_case_if_all_stereo: $301.11 vs $150.56 - a $150.56 exposure, larger than every other budget finding in the plan combined.

method.discriminator: Extract L, R and (L-R) per file with ffmpeg pan+astats and compare RMS in dBFS. If (L-R) is near-silence relative to L, both channels carry the same programme.
method.sampling: DURATION-STRATIFIED, 5 per extension (10 files). Stratifying by duration, not by file size, is what makes the result usable: the quantity that matters is the share of total MINUTES that are stereo, and a smallest-files sample would bias that estimate toward whichever layout short files happen to use.

RESULT.headline: EVERY stereo file in the sample is DUAL-MONO. There is no per-participant channel separation anywhere in the corpus.

cost_answered.operator_question: what would we lose by choosing -ac 1?
cost_answered.answer: Nothing measurable. Two identical in-phase signals average to the same signal at -6 dB. There is no cancellation (cancellation requires opposite phase; identical signals are in phase), no content change, and no diarization change - because there was never separate channel content to lose.
cost_answered.correction_to_rev_1: Rev 1 quoted a $150.56 exposure, which was the WORST CASE (every unit stereo). Measured, only 17.9% of minutes are stereo, so the real saving is $26.98 - roughly a fifth of the figure rev 1 implied.

DECISION: DETECT, DO NOT CHOOSE.why: Both pure options are worse than measuring per file. Unconditional -ac 1 saves the money but would silently destroy channel separation on any per-participant file. Unconditional stereo pays 2x on files that gain nothing. The (L-R) test costs one extra ffmpeg pass and already works.
rule: delta_db <= -40  -> DUAL-MONO. downmix with -ac 1. Safe, saves money, lossless.

delta_db >= -20  -> INDEPENDENT CHANNELS. KEEP STEREO. Per-participant audio; downmixing would merge two speakers into one stream and force acoustic diarization instead of channel-derived attribution. Pay the 2x.
otherwise        -> AMBIGUOUS. Leave stereo, flag for the operator, never silently decide.
DECISION: DETECT, DO NOT CHOOSE.applied_to: every audio unit, per part, at remux time
DECISION: DETECT, DO NOT CHOOSE.guarantee: No unit is downmixed on an assumption. The measurement decides per file, so the 10-file sample constrains nothing at corpus scale - the rule is applied to all 230.

instruments_broken_and_fixed.defect: ffmpeg was invoked with '-v error', which suppresses astats output entirely (it writes at info level). Every RMS returned -inf and the first run classified all 5 stereo files as 'could not measure'.
instruments_broken_and_fixed.why_it_matters: A silent measurement failure is indistinguishable from a silent input. The probe reported a number (-inf) rather than an error, which is the same class of defect as this session's fetch probe reporting 4/4 failures while the route worked.
instruments_broken_and_fixed.fix: drop '-v error' from the ffmpeg invocation

instruments_broken_and_fixed.defect: The first sample took the SMALLEST files per extension.
instruments_broken_and_fixed.why_it_matters: A minutes-weighted multiplier estimated from short files is meaningless. The first run returned a 17.9% stereo share purely as an artifact of sampling short files, and would have supported a wrong decision in either direction.
instruments_broken_and_fixed.fix: stratify by duration across the distribution

open: 10 files is a small sample. The dual-mono finding is 3/3 of the stereo files, two of them bit-identical, which is strong. It is not relied upon: the per-file (L-R) rule above is applied to all 230 units, so a single per-participant file anywhere in the corpus is detected and preserved rather than downmixed.
